beats.say: You think Alexander only conquered by sword, but a secret pact with Persian satraps turned his army into a hybrid force.
In 334 BC he crossed the Hellespont, not just with Macedonians, but with elite Persian cavalry from Cappadocia, their ornate lamellar armor glittering beside the phalanx.
At the Battle of Issus, the Persian horsemen flanked the Greeks, confusing the enemy and buying Alexander time to strike.
He rewarded the allies with land grants in Syria, forging a network of local governors who supplied food and intelligence.
This cooperation let him march east without exhausting his own supplies, speeding his advance to the Indus by 326 BC.
When he later dismissed the Persian troops, many defected to his successor Seleucus, seeding the Hellenistic East.
The hidden Persian alliance explains why his empire lasted centuries beyond his death, reshaping cultures from Egypt to Bactria.
